readme:
# LinkedIn Company Scraper

Enrich companies with data from their public [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com) company pages: employee count, industry, headquarters, description, specialties, website, founded year, follower count, exact LinkedIn member count, and (opt-in) recent company posts.

Give it a website domain, a company name or a LinkedIn link. No login or cookies needed, pay per result, and results that do not match are free.

## How It Works

1. If `linkedin_url` is provided, the actor extracts the company slug directly (recommended).
2. If not provided, the actor collects up to 4 candidate pages (company homepage link, Wikidata, name guesses, Bing, and as a last step at most one Google lookup), fetches each public page and checks that the page lists your website domain. When you give a name, the page name must also agree with it, otherwise the result is a mismatch. It stops at the first exact domain match, and skips the Google lookup when a page already matches the domain or clearly matches the name. When several company pages list the same website, or a page found by search carries extra words in its name (for example a university or fan page), the result is never marked as a domain match.
3. The actor scrapes the public LinkedIn guest page (`/organization-guest/company/{slug}`) which contains full company data in structured HTML. No login or cookies required.
4. Optionally scrapes the people page for employee profiles filtered by title.

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

Apify MCP server URL:

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/linkedin-company-scraper
```

Example prompt once connected:

> "Use `linkedin-company-scraper` to enrich these companies with LinkedIn data. Return the results as a table."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

## Input

```json
{
  "companies": [
    {
      "company_id": "acme-1",
      "company_name": "Example Company Ltd.",
      "linkedin_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/example-company"
    },
    {
      "company_id": "acme-2",
      "company_name": "Sample Widgets GmbH",
      "website_domain": "sample-widgets.example"
    }
  ],
  "domains": ["microsoft.com", "stripe.com"],
  "linkedinUrls": ["https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft"],
  "includePosts": true,
  "requestDelay": 3000
}
```

### Input Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `companies` | array | No | - | Companies to enrich. Objects, or plain text lines: a LinkedIn company URL, a website domain or URL, a universal name such as `mercedes-benz` (lowercase with dashes), or a company name. When unsure the actor treats a line as a name |
| `domains` | string[] | No | - | Website domains, one company each. Recommended, because the actor can check the match against the page |
| `linkedinUrls` | string[] | No | - | LinkedIn company URLs, one company each. Your URL is always kept in the result |
| `companies[].company_id` | string | No | - | Your internal identifier |
| `companies[].company_name` | string | No | - | Company name |
| `companies[].linkedin_url` | string | Recommended | - | Direct LinkedIn URL (skips search) |
| `companies[].website_domain` | string | No | - | Needed to find smaller companies reliably. Without it only large companies found via Wikidata or search are returned, unless `allowUnverifiedGuesses` is on |
| `includeEmployees` | boolean | No | `false` | Try the people page. Only returns rows with your own `linkedinCookie`; the public logged-out page has no employee list |
| `allowUnverifiedGuesses` | boolean | No | `false` | No longer used. Name-only companies are returned with `match_level` name_only |
| `includePosts` | boolean | No | `false` | Also return recent company posts from the public page (`recent_posts`) |
| `maxPostsPerCompany` | integer | No | `5` | Posts per company when `includePosts` is on (max 15) |
| `maxEmployeesPerCompany` | integer | No | `10` | Max employees per company (1-50) |
| `employeeTitleFilters` | string[] | No | `["HR","CEO","CTO","Recruiter","People","Talent"]` | Filter by title keywords |
| `requestDelay` | integer | No | `2000` | Delay between requests in ms. All requests to LinkedIn share one queue, so this is the minimum time between two LinkedIn requests, however many companies run at once |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer | No | `2` | How many companies are checked at the same time (1 to 3). Rows can arrive in a different order than your list; every row keeps its `company_id`. Runs with a LinkedIn login or employee scraping always check one company at a time |
| `linkedinCookie` | string | No | - | Optional li_at cookie for authenticated access (more data) |
| `linkedinEmail` | string | No | - | Optional: login to get li_at automatically |
| `linkedinPassword` | string | No | - | Optional: login password |

## Output

Each company produces one dataset row. Every row says how the company page was matched:

| `match_level` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `exact_domain` | The website on the LinkedIn page equals your domain (case, `www.` and path ignored) |
| `registrable_domain` | Same registrable domain, different host (a subdomain), or several company pages list the same website (see `match_note`) |
| `name_only` | No domain was given and the name is similar, or the same name on a different country domain (`match_note` says so) |
| `mismatch` | No page matched. The row has no company data, lists up to 3 other candidate pages in `alternatives`, and is not charged. These rows are saved in the `UNMATCHED_COMPANIES` key-value record, not in the dataset |

`match_confidence` keeps its earlier values (`verified`, `high`, `medium`, `low`) and is derived from `match_level`: `exact_domain` is `verified`, `registrable_domain` is `high`, `name_only` is `medium` when the name is nearly identical and no domain conflicts, otherwise `low`.

Unmatched companies (`mismatch`) are not charged and are not in the dataset. They are in the `UNMATCHED_COMPANIES` record of the run's key-value store. The run status line reads "X matched, Y unmatched (free, see UNMATCHED_COMPANIES)".

`matched_by` is `linkedin_url_input`, `domain`, `name` or `domain+name`. `lookup_source` is wikidata, homepage, google, bing, guess or direct. A LinkedIn URL you supply is always kept and its row is always returned. It is checked against the domain or name you gave with it: a conflict shows as `mismatch` with a note in `match_note`, and the row is still charged. With only a URL, `match_level` is null and `match_confidence` is null.

```json
{
  "company_id": "acme-1",
  "company_name": "Example Company Ltd.",
  "linkedin_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/example-company",
  "employee_count": 5000,
  "employee_count_range": "1,001-5,000",
  "industry": "Software Development",
  "headquarters": "Munich, Bavaria",
  "description": "Example Company Ltd. builds sample software for demo purposes.",
  "specialties": ["Sample Product", "Demo Service", "Widget Manufacturing"],
  "website": "https://www.example.com",
  "founded": "2015",
  "company_type": "Privately Held",
  "follower_count": 182760,
  "address": null,
  "tagline": "Help increase the GDP of the internet.",
  "logo_url": "https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/...",
  "employees_on_linkedin": 16694,
  "locations": ["354 Oyster Point Blvd, South San Francisco, California 94080, US"],
  "employees": [
    { "name": "Jane Doe", "title": "Head of People", "linkedin_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe-example" }
  ],
  "posts": [
    { "text": "We are hiring across our engineering teams.", "posted_at": "2d", "likes": null, "comments": null }
  ],
  "error": null
}
```

### Extracted Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `employee_count` | Upper bound of the size bucket (e.g., 5000 for "1,001-5,000"). LinkedIn only publishes a bucket here; for an exact figure use `employees_on_linkedin` |
| `employee_count_range` | Raw range string from LinkedIn |
| `industry` | Company industry |
| `headquarters` | City, Region |
| `description` | Full company description |
| `specialties` | List of specialties or focus areas |
| `website` | Company website URL |
| `founded` | Year founded |
| `company_type` | "Privately Held", "Public Company", etc. |
| `follower_count` | LinkedIn follower count |
| `tagline` | Short tagline under the company name |
| `logo_url` | Company logo image URL |
| `employees_on_linkedin` | Exact number of LinkedIn members listing the company as employer (the "N employees" figure on the page) |
| `locations` | Office location lines as text, as in earlier versions |
| `locations_detail` | The same locations as `{city, region, country, is_hq, address}`. Derived from the headquarters when the page lists none |
| `match_level` | `exact_domain`, `registrable_domain` or `name_only` (see above) |
| `universal_name` | The slug in the LinkedIn URL |
| `employee_count_min`, `employee_count_max` | Bounds of the size range (`max` is null for open ranges such as 10,001+) |
| `alternatives`, `match_note` | Other candidate pages and a short note on the match |
| `employees` | Empty unless you supply your own `linkedinCookie` and `includeEmployees` is on. The public page has no employee list |
| `recent_posts` | Recent company updates (text, age, reactions). Empty unless `includePosts` is `true` |

## Errors and partial results

A company that cannot be enriched (not found, blocked by LinkedIn, invalid URL, unresolvable numeric ID) is not added to the dataset and is not charged. It is listed in the key-value store record `FAILED_URLS` as `{url, company_id, reason}`, and the run status message counts them, for example "13 matched, 2 unmatched (free, see UNMATCHED_COMPANIES), 8 not found or failed (free, see FAILED_URLS)". If every company you provided is blocked by LinkedIn (403/429/451/authwall), the run ends as failed with a clear message. LinkedIn `/company/`, `/school/` and `/showcase/` URLs are accepted in any form (locale subdomains, query strings, trailing paths, upper case). If you start the actor with an empty input it enriches one built-in demo company (Microsoft).

If the run is about to hit its time limit, it stops cleanly. Companies that were not processed are not written to the dataset (so they are not charged). They are saved to the `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` record of the key-value store and the run status message says how many there are, so you can run them again. A company whose check takes too long is stopped, listed in `FAILED_URLS` and also in `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` with the reason `timeout`, so it can be run again. Every entry in `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` has a `reason` field (`timeout`, `time_limit` or `max_charge`). Entries in `companies` that cannot be used at all are listed in `INVALID_ENTRIES`.

If the charge for the next result would exceed the maximum total charge you set for the run, the run stops starting new companies. A company that is already being checked is only added if its result can still be charged. Every company that was not delivered is saved to the `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` record of the key-value store, and the status message reads "X matched, Y unmatched (free, see UNMATCHED_COMPANIES); stopped at your max charge, N not processed (see UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES)".

## Changelog

- 1.3.3: A company that takes too long to check is stopped, counted once as timed out in the final status message, and listed in `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` with the reason `timeout` as well as in `FAILED_URLS`. The final status message now also shows how many companies were not found or failed. Entries in `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES` have a `reason` field.
- 1.3: New input `maxConcurrency` (1 to 3, default 2) checks several companies at the same time; requests to LinkedIn still share one queue with the request delay between them, and the delay doubles for a minute after LinkedIn answers with a rate limit. Company websites are now fetched with settings that are remembered per website, so one site that blocks requests no longer slows down the others. When the maximum total charge you set is reached, the run stops starting new companies, does not add a result it cannot charge, and saves every company that was not delivered to `UNPROCESSED_COMPANIES`.
- 1.2: A website match no longer counts when the company name you gave has nothing in common with the page name. The lookup order is now homepage link, Wikidata, name guesses, Bing, then at most one Google lookup. Companies can now be given as a website domain, a name or a LinkedIn link. Each result says how the company page was matched (match_level) and lists other candidate pages, so a name alone no longer silently returns the wrong company. Results that do not match are returned free of charge. A LinkedIn link that redirects is reported as the page it lands on. Pages for schools or showcases are never reported as a domain match. New fields: universal_name, employee_count_min, employee_count_max, match_level, locations_detail, matched_by, alternatives, match_note. `match_confidence` and `locations` keep their earlier format; the new match levels are in `match_level` and the structured locations in `locations_detail`.

## Pricing

Pay-per-result via Apify Pay-Per-Event billing:

| Event | Price | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| Actor start | $0.001 | Charged once per run |
| Result | $0.005 | Charged per output row (each dataset item). Failed lookups are not pushed and not charged |

Enriching 1,000 companies costs about $5, all lookups included. No monthly fees.

## Numeric LinkedIn IDs

Older websites sometimes embed LinkedIn URLs in the numeric-ID form (for example `https://www.linkedin.com/company/19051`). LinkedIn walls those URLs behind a login page, so the actor probes a small set of candidate slugs built from `company_id` (typically the website domain) and `company_name`, and switches to the first slug URL that returns real company data. When this happens the output row sets `resolved_from_numeric_id: true`. If no candidate resolves, the company is listed in `FAILED_URLS` with reason `numeric_id_unresolvable` and is not charged.

## Tips

- Always provide `linkedin_url` when available. It is faster and more reliable than search.
- LinkedIn URLs can be found on company websites (footer or header links), Google Maps data, or business directories.
- The LinkedIn slug often differs from the legal company name (e.g., "Example Company AG" may map to `example-company`, not `example-company-ag`).
- Use `requestDelay: 3000` or higher to avoid rate limiting (HTTP 999).
- Connection handling is built in, nothing to configure.

## Use Cases

- B2B Lead Enrichment: add employee counts, industry, and HQ to your company database.
- Sales Intelligence: size a company precisely with `employees_on_linkedin` and read its recent posts for talking points.
- Market Research: analyze industry distribution, company sizes, and specialties across a list of companies.

## FAQ

**Will it match the wrong company?**
It tries hard not to. When you give a website domain, a page only counts as a domain match if it lists that same website, and the page name must agree with the name you gave. Pages that do not pass are returned as `mismatch` in the `UNMATCHED_COMPANIES` record, are not added to the dataset and are not charged. When several company pages use the same website, or the name alone is the only evidence, `match_level` says `name_only` and `alternatives` lists the other candidates, so you can check them yourself. For a checked match, give the website domain.

**What should I put in `companies`?**
One entry per company: a website domain (`ikea.com`), a company name (`Siemens Healthineers`) or a LinkedIn company link. You can also pass objects with `company_id`, `company_name`, `website_domain` and `linkedin_url`, as in earlier versions.

**What happens with a LinkedIn link I give myself?**
The actor uses that page and always returns it. If you also give a domain or name, it checks them against the page and reports the result in `match_level`. With only a link, `match_level` is empty and `match_note` says it was not checked.

**Do I need a LinkedIn account?**
No. The actor reads the public company page. The optional login fields are only for the employee list feature.
